result.title: Honest but Wrong: Formalizing Retraction in the Ethics of Speech Acts
result.comment: To appear in Proceedings of the Workshop on Verifying Law and Ethics, and Legal Autoformalisation (VLE-LEGATO 2026), JURIX 2026
result.summary: A speaker who asserts honestly may later discover that its assertion was false. Such erroneous truths are not lies, yet they raise the question of whether, and on which moral grounds, the speaker must retract them. Using the FIPA-ACL performative disconfirm, we extend a belief-based framework that evaluates speech acts under deontologism and consequentialism to the case of retraction. We prove that the honesty duty of deontologism, which bears on utterances when they are made, never requires retracting an erroneous truth, and add a persistent one, which forbids letting the addressee believe what the speaker no longer believes. On a legal-advice case implemented in Answer Set Programming, we show that deontologism and consequentialism both require the retraction, but that consequentialism no longer does once it comes too late to prevent harm.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从言语行为伦理角度形式化「撤回」：用 FIPA-ACL 的 disconfirm 扩展基于信念的框架，区分道义论与后果论，并证明仅在说话时生效的诚实义务永不要求撤回无心的错误断言，需另加持续义务；并在 ASP 实现的法律咨询案例中比较两种立场何时要求撤回。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关联，但其「说话后信念改变即须纠正听者信念」的持续义务与撤回时机—代价分析，或可启发多模态推理系统何时应撤销已给出的结论、以及延迟纠正的代价如何评价，可供核查。
